paragraphs.sourceText: (1) New calls for Australia to introduce a sugar-sweetened beverages tax have sparked an outcry from the food and beverage industry and provoked resistance from politicians. But why do health experts keep calling for a sugar-sweetened beverages (SSB) tax, and why are politicians and industry resisting it?
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 澳大利亚开征含糖饮料税的新呼声引发了食品饮料行业的强烈抗议，并引发了政界人士的抵制。但为什么健康专家一直呼吁征收含糖饮料（SSB）税，而政客和业界又为何抵制呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Sugar taxes vary in design around the world in 26 countries. In Mexico, a 10%tax on sugary drinks was introduced in 2014.When the tax starts in the UK in April, there will be two bands — one for sugar content above 5g per 100ml and a second, higher tax on drinks containing more than 8g of sugar per 100ml.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 世界各地 26 个国家的糖税设计各不相同。墨西哥于 2014 年开始对含糖饮料征收 10% 的税。当英国 4 月份开始征税时，将有两个等级——第一个等级针对每 100 毫升含糖量超过 5 克的饮料，第二个等级针对每 100 毫升含糖量超过 8 克的饮料征税。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) In a 2018 statement on nutrition the Australian Medical Association(AMA)urged the government to introduce an SSB tax. This is significant because AMA is generally conservative when it comes to health policy and often avoids controversial debates. But it now wants a sugar tax “as a matter of priority”.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 澳大利亚医学协会 (AMA) 在 2018 年营养声明中敦促政府征收 SSB 税。这一点很重要，因为 AMA 在卫生政策方面通常比较保守，并且经常避免有争议的辩论。但它现在希望“作为优先事项”征收糖税。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The health minister has made it clear the government will not support it, saying food labelling laws and voluntary codes of conduct to restrict food marketing to children are adequate. A Labor MP also stopped short of supporting a tax, saying other strategies are needed to promote a healthy lifestyle. The Greens, led by former doctor Richard Di Natale, support the tax and have previously proposed a 20%increase to the price of sugary drinks.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 卫生部长已明确表示政府不会支持，称食品标签法和限制向儿童推销食品的自愿行为准则已经足够。一位工党议员也不支持征税，称需要采取其他策略来促进健康的生活方式。由前医生理查德·迪·纳塔莱 (Richard Di Natale) 领导的绿党支持这项税收，并此前提议将含糖饮料的价格提高 20%。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) According to Prof. Tim Gill, from the Boden Institute of Obesity, Nutrition, Exercise &Eating Disorders in Sydney, the strength of an SSB tax is that it targets an easily defined product. “It’s easy to identify sugary drinks and their manufacturers, and you can tax them at their production,” he said. “There are a limited number of sugary drinks producers in Australia. A problem for governments collecting taxes can be how complicated it can be. If you were to try to tax every sugary food for example, that would be very complicated to do.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 悉尼博登肥胖、营养、运动和饮食失调研究所的 Tim Gill 教授表示，SSB 税的优势在于它针对的是易于定义的产品。 “很容易识别含糖饮料及其制造商，你可以在生产时对他们征税，”他说。 “澳大利亚的含糖饮料生产商数量有限。政府征税的一个问题可能是它的复杂性。例如，如果你试图对每种含糖食品征税，那将是非常复杂的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) The government has previously used complexity as an argument against an SSB tax. “But now with the UK jumping on the bandwagon, which has a similar consumption culture to ours but with a larger population and more producers, that complexity argument doesn’t hold weight anymore,” Gill said.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 政府此前曾以复杂性作为反对 SSB 税的理由。 “但现在随着英国加入这股潮流，它与我们有着相似的消费文化，但拥有更多的人口和更多的生产者，这种复杂性的论点不再有效，”吉尔说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Bureau of Statistics data shows Australia is one of the 10 highest soft drink-consuming countries per capita. The World Health Organisation recommends adults consume no more than six teaspoons of sugar per day, but the average Australian consumes more than double that. A 330ml bottle of Coke contains nine teaspoons of sugar.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 统计局数据显示，澳大利亚是人均软饮料消费量最高的10个国家之一。世界卫生组织建议成年人每天摄入的糖量不超过六茶匙，但澳大利亚人的平均摄入量是这个数字的两倍多。一瓶 330 毫升的可乐含有九茶匙糖。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) A study published in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics found sales of soft drinks in Melbourne’s Alfred hospital dropped 27.6%during a 17-week trial when the price of sugary drinks was increased by 20%. Bottled water sales increased by almost the same amount.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 发表在《营养与饮食学院杂志》上的一项研究发现，在为期 17 周的试验中，当含糖饮料的价格上涨 20% 时，墨尔本阿尔弗雷德医院的软饮料销量下降了 27.6%。瓶装水销量增长几乎相同。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) An analysis of sugary-drink purchases in Mexico conducted two years after the tax was introduced found a
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 税收征收两年后对墨西哥含糖饮料购买情况进行的分析发现

paragraphs.sourceText: 5.5% drop in the first year, followed by a 9.7%decline in the second. While two years is not enough to determine the long-term impact on health, the study found: “These reductions in consumption could have positive impacts on health outcomes and reductions in healthcare expenses.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 第一年下降 5.5%，第二年下降 9.7%。虽然两年不足以确定对健康的长期影响，但研究发现：“消费的减少可能对健康结果和医疗费用的减少产生积极影响。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) Sugar-sweetened drinks and sugar generally have been associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, tooth decay and bone density problems. The Australian Healthcare and Hospitals Association says obesity is the leading cause of preventable death or illness in Australia — above smoking. But it will take longer term analysis to see clear evidence of any impact of a tax on obesity levels.
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) 含糖饮料和糖通常与肥胖、2 型糖尿病、心血管疾病、蛀牙和骨密度问题有关。澳大利亚医疗保健和医院协会表示，肥胖是澳大利亚可预防的死亡或疾病的主要原因，仅次于吸烟。但需要更长期的分析才能看到税收对肥胖水平产生影响的明确证据。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) Lobby groups from the food and beverage industry are powerful. The Australian Beverages Council, the industry’s lobby group, has been fighting against a tax for years. It says there is no evidence a tax will do anything to reduce obesity, and it will cost jobs, which is a frightening message for politicians. The Australasian Association of Convenience Stores (AACS)described the introduction of an SSB tax in the UK as “lazy,” “flawed,” “discriminatory” and “irrational”. It has ramped up its campaign to prevent such a tax in Australia.
paragraphs.translationZh: (11)食品饮料行业的游说团体势力强大。该行业的游说团体澳大利亚饮料委员会多年来一直在反对税收。报告称，没有证据表明税收对减少肥胖有任何作用，而且还会减少就业机会，这对政客来说是一个可怕的信息。澳大利亚便利店协会 (AACS) 将英国引入 SSB 税形容为“懒惰”、“有缺陷”、“歧视性”和“不合理”。它已加大力度阻止澳大利亚征收此类税。

paragraphs.sourceText: (12) Would introducing a sugar tax make Australia a nanny-state? It depends on whether you believe the food and beverage industry has too much power. Health experts argue that through advertising, product placement and political influence, the food and beverage industry has an unfair and non-transparent influence over consumer purchasing habits, and that children especially are sometimes powerless to recognise or resist it. They say an SSB tax would hold the industry to account. Others argue people need to take personal responsibility.
paragraphs.translationZh: (12) 引入糖税会让澳大利亚成为保姆国家吗？这取决于您是否认为食品和饮料行业的权力太大。健康专家认为，食品饮料行业通过广告、植入式广告和政治影响力，对消费者的购买习惯产生不公平和不透明的影响，尤其是儿童有时无法识别或抵制。他们表示，SSB 税将使该行业承担责任。其他人则认为人们需要承担个人责任。

paragraphs.sourceText: (13) A Deakin University study used economic modelling to show the increase in annual spending on sugar-sweetened drinks under a 20%tax would average $30 a person, but those in the lowest socioeconomic groups would pay $5 a year more than those in the wealthiest groups.
paragraphs.translationZh: (13) 迪肯大学的一项研究使用经济模型表明，在 20% 的税收下，每人每年在含糖饮料上的支出将平均增加 30 美元，但社会经济地位最低的群体每年将比最富有群体多支付 5 美元。

paragraphs.sourceText: (14) Researchers concluded this was a modest price to pay given the benefits — and that Australia’s lowest socioeconomic group would receive the greatest health benefits. Health experts and advocacy groups say governments could reduce the financial burden on disadvantaged people by using revenue from a tax to fund health initiatives.
paragraphs.translationZh: (14) 研究人员得出的结论是，考虑到所带来的好处，这是一个适中的价格，而且澳大利亚社会经济地位最低的群体将获得最大的健康福利。卫生专家和倡导团体表示，政府可以通过利用税收收入资助卫生举措来减轻弱势群体的经济负担。

paragraphs.translationZh: 11.澳大利亚政府对SSB税有何反应？

paragraphs.translationZh: 12.以下哪个组织反对SSB税？

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) I’d been living in Los Angeles just under a year when, in the spring of 1983, I answered an ad in the Hollywood Reporter for a receptionist and got the job. The pay wasn’t much, but the work was in “the Business” — an apt Los Angeles euphemism for the entertainment industry. The location was within bicycling distance of my home, and they only wanted someone to work mornings. I’d get off by 1 p.m., which I thought would leave me plenty of time to do my own writing. I was wrong about that. The place was so frantic I’d come out wired and need the rest of the day to simply calm down. When, after about two weeks, I realized my afternoons were being spent in activities equivalent to running around the block twenty or thirty times, I asked to be put on full-time. Since I wasn’t getting anything else, why not, I figured, jump in for the total experience
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 1983 年春天，我在洛杉矶生活了不到一年，我应聘《好莱坞报道》上的一则接待员招聘广告，并得到了这份工作。薪水不多，但工作是在“商业”——这是洛杉矶对娱乐业的一个恰当的委婉说法。该地点距离我家不远，骑自行车即可到达，他们只希望有人在早上工作。我会在下午 1 点之前下班，我想这会给我留下足够的时间来写我自己的文章。我错了。这个地方太疯狂了，我一出来就紧张起来，需要这一天剩下的时间来冷静下来。大约两周后，当我意识到我的下午都花在相当于绕着街区跑二十或三十次的活动上时，我要求全职工作。既然我没有得到任何其他东西，我想为什么不加入到整体体验中呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The (still thriving) company I found myself a part of possessed the unlikely name of Breakdown Services, Ltd. During the six months I worked there, I learned to savor all of that phrase’s more cynical reverberations, but in terms of the job it dealt with the dismantling or breakdown of television and film scripts. Scripts gathered from producers or studios would be regurgitated (回流) by Breakdown in the form of plot summaries, character descriptions, number of scenes per character, and the number of dialogue lines each speaks. These compilations were then xeroxed and distributed to hundreds of subscribing actors’ agents who proceeded to submit their clients for likely parts. It was a process, as I was to discover by way of angry phone calls when “breakdowns” arrived late or not at all, that the agents regarded with a reverence others might reserve for morning prayer.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 我发现自己所在的那家（仍在蓬勃发展的）公司拥有一个不太可能的名字：Breakdown Services, Ltd.。在我在那里工作的六个月里，我学会了品味这个短语所有更愤世嫉俗的反响，但就其涉及拆除或分解电视和电影剧本的工作而言。从制片人或工作室收集的脚本将通过 Breakdown 以情节摘要、角色描述、每个角色的场景数以及每个角色的对话行数的形式回流（回流）。然后，这些汇编被复印并分发给数百名订阅演员的经纪人，他们继续向他们的客户提交可能的部分。当“故障”迟到或根本没有出现时，我通过愤怒的电话发现，这是一个过程，特工们以其他人可能为晨祷保留的崇敬态度对待。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Breakdown Services, Ltd. was the brainchild of a young man named Gary Marsh. Gary was twenty- eight when I met him, but he’d founded Breakdown when he was eighteen and was considered something of an entrepreneurial prodigy. His mother was an agent and he’d observed the piles of scripts she and her agent pals had to plow through in order to match a given role with the talent they represented. He’d also observed how much they hated the reading part of their jobs and had cleverly devised breakdowns as a way of extracting the material they needed.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) Breakdown Services, Ltd. 是一位名叫加里·马什 (Gary Marsh) 的年轻人的创意。我见到加里时他才 28 岁，但他在 18 岁时就创立了 Breakdown，被认为是一位创业神童。他的母亲是一名经纪人，他观察到她和她的经纪人朋友必须仔细研究成堆的剧本，以便将给定的角色与他们所代表的才华相匹配。他还观察到他们多么讨厌工作中的阅读部分，并巧妙地设计了细分作为提取所需材料的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) By the time I arrived, five full-time breakdown writers worked in a desk-lined back room overlooking a parking lot. I’ve heard the current crew has now advanced to computers, but when I was there typewriters were the norm. When they weren’t typing, the writers would curl up on the office’s worn stuffed couch and, with a script propped against one arm, fill legal-sized yellow pads with dialogue line numbers and comments which they’d then type up. It could be a complex job. For example, the breakdown for a film originally called Teenage Gambler lists over forty characters, ranging from the teenaged gambling leader to five waiters who sing “Happy Birthday” at a surprise party.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 当我到达时，五名全职故障分析作家在一间摆着桌子的后面房间里工作，俯瞰着停车场。我听说现在的工作人员已经升级到使用计算机，但当我在那里时，打字机是常态。当他们不打字的时候，编剧们会蜷缩在办公室破旧的填充沙发上，用一只手臂支撑着一份剧本，在法定大小的黄色便笺簿上填写对话行编号和评论，然后将它们打印出来。这可能是一项复杂的工作。例如，一部最初名为《少年赌徒》的电影的细目列出了四十多个角色，从少年赌博头目到在惊喜派对上唱“生日快乐”的五名服务员。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Perhaps because of the patience involved in this sort of extraction, women seemed to dominate the ranks of the break-downers (during my tenure the ratio was four to one). Although Gary knew I’d done a bit of writing, I was relegated to the front office and never received an invitation to try my hand at breakdowns. It wasn’t something I really wanted to do. For one thing, the writers were a youthful bunch. The back room senior was in her early thirties, but none of the others had hit twenty-five. And I think Gary rightly surmised I’d be too openly cynical for the job or try to embellish too much. Breakdowns were produced anonymously and offered no artistic evaluations of the scripts. The writers might talk among themselves about a piece they felt was particularly good or bad, but such editorializing was not allowed to make its way into the final product. That this restriction was frustrating is indicated by the fact that two of the writers began venting opinions as moonlighting theater critics for small local papers.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 也许是因为这种提取需要耐心，女性似乎在破坏者队伍中占主导地位（在我任职期间，这一比例为四比一）。尽管加里知道我已经写了一些文章，但我还是被调到了前台，并且从未收到过尝试解决故障的邀请。这不是我真正想做的事情。一方面，编剧是一群年轻的人。里屋的前辈三十岁出头，其他人都还没到二十五岁。我认为加里正确地推测我对这份工作过于公开愤世嫉俗，或者试图过度粉饰。分解是匿名制作的，并且没有对剧本进行艺术评价。作家们可能会互相谈论他们认为特别好或特别坏的作品，但这样的社论不允许进入最终产品。两位作家开始以兼职戏剧评论家的身份为当地小报纸发表观点，这一事实表明这种限制令人沮丧。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) For Gary, the most problematical aspect of the breakdown business was its limited market. This had nothing to do with his operating methodology; he did what he could to exploit the possibilities. Each weekday a hardy crew made predawn deliveries of breakdowns to agents’ homes or offices, while a post-dawn quartet of pager-equipped Breakdown field workers haunted the big studios ready to pounce on an available script. For these studio prowlers speed was of the essence, not only because Hollywood tends to be crisis-prone and wants everything done quickly, but because a rival, spawned by the success of Breakdown Services, Ltd. and infuriatingly named BreakThrough Productions, Ltd., was also on the hunt.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 对于Gary来说，故障业务最大的问题是市场有限。这与他的操作方法无关，而是与他的操作方法无关。他尽其所能地利用各种可能性。每个工作日，坚强的工作人员都会在黎明前将故障报告送到特工的家中或办公室，而黎明后，四名配备传呼机的故障现场工作人员则出没于大型工作室，准备抓住可用的剧本。对于这些制片厂徘徊者来说，速度至关重要，不仅因为好莱坞容易发生危机并希望一切都能快速完成，而且因为 Breakdown Services, Ltd. 的成功催生了一个竞争对手，它的名字令人恼火地命名为 BreakThrough Productions, Ltd.，也在寻找。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Breakdown Services unquestionably dominated the field, but the field itself had immutable perimeters. Breakdown’s subscribers had to be accredited agents, though there were some exceptions to this rule. For instance, specialized media organizations, such as the competitive, vulture-like companies that insured movie productions, could keep tabs on the industry by subscribing to the weekly Breakdown summaries. But the whole Breakdown operation was hard to monitor. When I was there, a Breakdown subscription was expensive, something like $500 a year. And though breakdowns were copyrighted and unauthorized reproduction was clearly prohibited, xerox machines are notoriously bad at picking up such distinctions and among the larger agencies breakdowns were undoubtedly duplicated and passed around.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 故障服务无疑占据了该领域的主导地位，但该领域本身的边界是不可改变的。 Breakdown 的订户必须是经过认可的代理商，但这一规则也有一些例外。例如，专业媒体组织，例如为电影制作提供保险的竞争激烈的秃鹰公司，可以通过订阅每周的细分摘要来密切关注该行业。但整个故障操作很难监控。当我在那里的时候，Breakdown 订阅很贵，大约每年 500 美元。尽管故障是受版权保护的，并且明确禁止未经授权的复制，但众所周知，复印机在识别此类区别方面表现不佳，而且在较大的机构中，故障无疑会被复制和传播。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Gary’s response to these built-in economic dilemmas was to diversify. A separate department for commercials, for example, appeared as part of the Breakdown menu. Although Breakdown staffers were supposed to refrain from giving tips to potential talent, I did once tell a friend — who hoped to finance the college educations of her five-year-old identical twins by getting them on a commercial — that a juice company had put out a call for identical twin girls. Their agent submitted them, but they didn’t get the job. The nightly Breakdown delivery system expanded to an all-day messenger service. Gary also made available an assortment of directories and mailing labels listing casting directors, talent agents, and literary agents in Los Angeles and New York. The current Breakdown brochure adds yet another Breakdown amenity; for fifteen dollars you can receive an “actors’ relaxation” cassette tape “designed to maximize your abilities and stimulate your creative senses”.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 加里对这些内在的经济困境的反应是多元化。例如，一个单独的广告部门作为“细分”菜单的一部分出现。尽管 Breakdown 的员工应该避免向潜在人才提供提示，但我曾经告诉一位朋友——她希望通过让她五岁的同卵双胞胎上广告来资助她们的大学教育——一家果汁公司已经发出了招募同卵双胞胎女孩的号召。他们的经纪人向他们提交了申请，但他们没有得到这份工作。每晚的故障传送系统扩展到全天的信使服务。加里还提供了各种各样的目录和邮寄标签，列出了洛杉矶和纽约的选角导演、人才经纪人和文学经纪人。当前的故障手册增加了另一个故障便利设施；只要花十五美元，你就可以收到一盘“演员放松”盒式磁带，“旨在最大限度地发挥你的能力并激发你的创造力”。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) It was delightful to be in such a place, after long weeks of daily and nightly familiarity with miners’ cabins — with all which this implies of dirt floor, never-made beds, tin plates and cups, bacon and beans and black coffee, and nothing of ornament but war pictures from the Eastern illustrated papers tacked to the log walls. That was all hard, cheerless, materialistic desolation, but here was a nest which had aspects to rest the tired eyes and refresh that something in one’s nature which, after long fasting, recognizes, when confronted by the belongings of art, howsoever cheap and modest they may be, that it has unconsciously been famishing and now has found nourishment.
paragraphs.translationZh: （1）在连续数周的日日夜夜熟悉矿工小屋之后，来到这样一个地方真是令人高兴——这一切意味着肮脏的地板、从未整理过的床、锡盘和杯子、培根、豆子和黑咖啡，除了钉在原木墙上的东方插图报纸上的战争图片外，没有任何装饰。这一切都是艰苦、沉闷、唯物主义的荒凉，但这里有一个巢穴，它可以让疲惫的眼睛得到休息，也可以使人的本性中的某种东西焕然一新，这种本性在长期禁食之后，会认识到，当面对艺术品时，无论它们多么廉价和朴素，它已经无意识地挨饿了，现在已经找到了营养。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) I could not have believed that a rag carpet could feast me so, and so content me; or that there could be such solace to the soul in wall-paper and framed lithographs (平版印刷画), and bright-colored tidies and lamp- mats, and Windsor chairs, and varnished whatnots (陈设架), with sea-shells and books and china vases on them, and the score of little unclassifiable tricks and touches that a woman’s hand distributes about a home, which one sees without knowing he sees them, yet would miss in a moment if they were taken away. The delight that was in my heart showed in my face, and the man saw it and was pleased; saw it so plainly that he answered it as if it had been spoken.
paragraphs.translationZh: （2）我简直不敢相信一块破地毯能让我如此满足，如此满足；或者说，墙纸和镶框石版画、色彩鲜艳的桌布和灯垫、温莎椅、涂漆的陈设架、上面放着贝壳、书籍和瓷器花瓶，还有女人的手在家里散布的一些无法分类的小技巧和触摸，这些东西可以给灵魂带来安慰，人们看到这些，却不知道自己看到了它们，但也能得到心灵的慰藉。如果他们被带走的话，就想念一下。我心里的喜悦表现在脸上，那人看见了，也很高兴。他看得如此清楚，以至于他的回答就像是有人说出来的一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) “All her work,” he said, caressingly; “she did it all herself — every bit,” and he took the room in with a glance which was full of affectionate worship. One of those soft Japanese fabrics with which women drape with careful negligence the upper part of a picture-frame was out of adjustment. He noticed it, and rearranged it with cautious pains, stepping back several times to gauge the effect before he got it to suit him. Then he gave it a light finishing pat or two with his hand, and said: “She always does that. You can’t tell just what it lacks, but it does lack something until you’ve done that — you can see it yourself after it’s done, but that is all you know; you can’t find out the law of it. It’s like the finishing pats a mother gives the child’s hair after she’s got it combed and brushed, I reckon. I’ve seen her fix all these things so much that I can do them all just her way, though I don’t know the law of any of them. But she knows the law. She knows the why and the how both; but I don’t know the why; I only know the how.”
paragraphs.translationZh: （3）“都是她的作品，”他爱抚地说； “这一切都是她自己做的——每一点，”他用充满深情崇拜的目光扫视了整个房间。一种柔软的日本布料，女人们小心翼翼地把它挂在相框的上半部分，但这种布料已经不合适了。他注意到了这一点，小心翼翼地重新安排了它，后退了几次以衡量效果，然后才找到适合他的。然后他用手轻轻地拍了一两下，说道：“她总是这样做。你无法分辨它缺少什么，但在你这样做之前，它确实缺少一些东西——完成后你可以自己看到它，但这就是你所知道的；你无法找出它的规律。我想，这就像母亲在梳理和梳理孩子的头发后对孩子的头发进行最后的拍打一样。我见过她修复所有这些东西，所以我可以按照她的方式去做，尽管我不知道其中任何一个的法则，但她知道为什么，也知道如何做；但我不知道为什么，我只知道如何做。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) He took me into a bedroom so that I might wash my hands; such a bedroom as I had not seen for years: white counterpane, white pillows, carpeted floor, papered walls, pictures, dressing-table, with mirror and pin-cushion and dainty toilet things; and in the corner a wash-stand, with real china-ware bowl and pitcher, and with soap in a china dish, and on a rack more than a dozen towels — towels too clean and white for one out of practice to use without some vague sense of profanation. So my face spoke again, and he answered with gratified words: “All her work; she did it all herself — every bit. Nothing here that hasn’t felt the touch of her hand. Now you would think — But I mustn’t talk so much.”
paragraphs.translationZh: （4）他把我带到卧室让我洗手；我已经好几年没见过这样的卧室了：白色的床单、白色的枕头、铺着地毯的地板、贴着纸的墙壁、照片、梳妆台、镜子、针垫和精致的盥洗用具。角落里有一个盥洗台，上面放着真正的瓷碗和水罐，瓷盘里放着肥皂，架子上放着十几条毛巾——这些毛巾太干净太白了，对于一个不熟练的人来说，使用起来不会没有某种模糊的亵渎感。于是我的脸又说话了，他用满意的话语回答道：“所有的工作都是她自己做的——一点一滴。这里的一切都感受到了她的手的触摸。现在你会想——但我不应该说那么多。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) By this time I was wiping my hands and glancing from detail to detail of the room’s belongings, as one is apt to do when he is in a new place, where everything he sees is a comfort to his eye and his spirit; and I became conscious, in one of those unaccountable ways, you know, that there was something there somewhere that the man wanted me to discover for myself. I knew it perfectly, and I knew he was trying to help me by furtive indications with his eye, so I tried hard to get on the right track, being eager to gratify him. I failed several times, as I could see 5
paragraphs.translationZh: （5）此时，我正在擦手，逐个查看房间里的物品，就像一个人到了一个新地方时很容易做的那样，在那里他看到的一切对他的眼睛和精神来说都是一种安慰；我意识到，以一种无法解释的方式，你知道，那个男人想让我亲自去发现某些东西。我心里很清楚，我知道他是想用眼神暗中暗示来帮助我，所以我努力走上正轨，渴望让他满意。我失败了好几次，我可以看到 5

paragraphs.sourceText: out of the corner of my eye without being told; but at last I knew I must be looking straight at the thing — knew it from the pleasure issuing in invisible waves from him. He broke into a happy laugh, and rubbed his hands together, and cried out: “That’s it! You’ve found it. I knew you would. It’s her picture.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 没有被告知就从我的眼角消失；但最后我知道我一定是在直视那东西——从他身上发出的无形的快乐中知道这一点。他高兴地大笑起来，搓着手，喊道：“就是它了！你找到了。我就知道你会找到的。这是她的照片。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (6)I went to the little black-walnut bracket on the farther wall, and did find there what I had not yet noticed — a picture case. It contained the sweetest girlish face, and the most beautiful, as it seemed to me, that I had ever seen. The man drank the admiration from my face, and was fully satisfied.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6)我走到远处墙上的黑胡桃木小支架前，确实在那里发现了我没有注意到的东西——一个画盒。它有着一张最甜美的少女脸，在我看来也是我所见过的最美丽的脸。男人从我脸上流露出钦佩之情，心满意足。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) “Nineteen her last birthday,” he said, as he put the picture back; “and that was the day we were married. When you see her — ah, just wait till you see her!”
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) “她上一次生日十九岁，”他边说边把照片放回去； “那就是我们结婚的那天。当你看到她时——啊，等着瞧吧！”

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) “Where is she? When will she be in?”
paragraphs.translationZh: (8)“她在哪儿？她什么时候来？”

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) “Oh, she’s away now. She’s gone to see her people. They live forty or fifty miles from here. She’s been gone two weeks today.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) “哦，她现在走了。她去看她的人了。他们住在离这里四十或五十英里的地方。她今天已经走了两个星期了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) “When do you expect her back?”
paragraphs.translationZh: (10)“你预计她什么时候回来？”

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) “This is Wednesday. She’ll be back Saturday, in the evening — about nine o’clock, likely.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) “今天是星期三。她会在星期六晚上回来——可能是九点左右。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (12) I felt a sharp sense of disappointment.
paragraphs.translationZh: (12) 我感到一种强烈的失望感。

paragraphs.sourceText: (13) “I’m sorry, because I’ll be gone then,” I said, regretfully.
paragraphs.translationZh: (13) “对不起，因为那时我就要走了。”我遗憾地说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (14) “Gone? No — why should you go? Don’t go. She’ll be disappointed.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (14)“走了？不——你为什么要走？别走。她会失望的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (15) She would be disappointed — that beautiful creature! If she had said the words herself, they could hardly have blessed me more. I was feeling a deep, strong longing to see her — a longing so supplicating, so insistent, that it made me afraid. I said to myself: “I will go straight away from this place, for my peace of mind’s sake.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (15) 她会失望的——那个美丽的生物！如果这些话是她自己说的，他们对我的祝福就再多不过了。我感到一种深深而强烈的渴望见到她——一种如此恳求、如此强烈的渴望，以至于让我感到害怕。我对自己说：“为了内心的平静，我要立刻离开这个地方。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (16) “You see, she likes to have people come and stop with us — people who know things, and can talk — people like you. She delights in it; for she knows — oh, she knows nearly everything herself, and can talk, oh, like a bird — and the books she reads, why, you would be astonished. Don’t go; it’s only a little while, you know, and she’ll be so disappointed.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (16) “你看，她喜欢有人来和我们一起停留——那些知道事情、能说话的人——像你这样的人。她很高兴；因为她知道——哦，她自己几乎知道一切，而且能说话，哦，像鸟一样——还有她读的书，为什么，你会感到惊讶。别走；只有一会儿，你知道，她会很失望。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (17) I heard the words, but hardly noticed them, I was so deep in my thinkings and strugglings. He left me, but I didn’t know. Presently he was back, with the picture case in his hand, and he held it open before me and said: “There, now, tell her to her face you could have stayed to see her, and you wouldn’t.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (17) 我听到了这句话，但几乎没有注意到它们，我陷入了深深的思考和挣扎中。他离开了我，但我却不知道。不久他回来了，手里拿着相框，他在我面前打开它，说道：“好了，现在，当面告诉她，你本来可以留下来见她，但你不会。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Students aiming to enter one of the top universities in China this year had better be able to swim or be prepared to learn swimming and pass a swim test since this university will not grant bachelor’s degrees if they cannot swim.

paragraphs.sourceText: This September, would-be freshmen at the university will have to take swimming courses if they fail a swimming test at the beginning of their university life. And they won’t receive their degrees if they cannot swim before their graduation, in accordance with a message at a university staff meeting days ago, a local newspaper reported on Monday.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今年九月，如果大学新生在大学生活之初未能通过游泳考试，他们将必须参加游泳课程。据当地一家报纸周一报道，几天前在一次大学教职员工会议上发布的信息显示，如果他们在毕业前不会游泳，他们将无法获得学位。

paragraphs.sourceText: As to why the university is linking swimming ability with degrees, “as a requisite survival skill, swimming is beneficial for students in the long run, since swimming is helpful in improving students’ endurance and doing less harm to joints and muscles as a water sport,” said head of the Division of Sports Science and Physical Education
paragraphs.translationZh: 至于为什么学校将游泳能力与学位挂钩，“作为一项必备的生存技能，从长远来看，游泳对学生是有益的，因为游泳有助于提高学生的耐力，并减少作为水上运动对关节和肌肉的伤害，”运动科学与体育学部负责人说

paragraphs.sourceText: Viewing the ability to swim as a must for students to earn their degrees is not new in this top university, as this ability was listed on its school regulations in the early 20th century.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这所顶尖大学中，将游泳能力视为学生获得学位的必备条件并不新鲜，因为这项能力早在 20 世纪初期就被列入学校规定中。

paragraphs.sourceText: “As early as 90 years ago, the university required that students cannot graduate from the university or study overseas if they cannot swim, though the requirement didn’t work later on since the swimming pools at the campus could not accommodate increasingly more students,” said the head of the Sports Science and Physical Education Division.
paragraphs.translationZh: “早在90年前，学校就规定，不会游泳的学生不能毕业或出国留学，但后来这个要求没有发挥作用，因为校园的游泳池无法容纳越来越多的学生。”体育科学与体育处处长说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many alumni of this university had to meet the swimming challenge. The university is not the first university to require swimming as a compulsory course. Other universities in China have also listed swimming as a compulsory course for students.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这所大学的许多校友都必须接受游泳挑战。该大学并不是第一所将游泳作为必修课的大学。国内其他大学也将游泳列为学生的必修课。

paragraphs.sourceText: University of Chicago nixes nearly 60-year-old swim requirements
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥大学取消近60岁老人游泳要求

paragraphs.sourceText: For almost 60 years, one of the first things new students had to prove at the University of Chicago was their ability to stay afloat.
paragraphs.translationZh: 近 60 年来，新生在芝加哥大学首先要证明的事情之一就是他们维持生计的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: But students in the Class of 2016 wouldn’t have to pass a swim test or take a swimming course in their freshman year. The University of Chicago has joined other universities in nixing the requirement.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但 2016 届学生在大一时不必通过游泳考试或参加游泳课程。芝加哥大学与其他大学一起取消了这一要求。

paragraphs.sourceText: A handful of universities still require swimming tests to graduate, a dramatic shift considering that in 1977, 42 percent of colleges had some sort of swimming requirement, the Associated Press reported in 2006.By 1982 that figure had plummeted to 8 percent, and today, there are just a handful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 据美联社 2006 年报道，少数大学仍然要求通过游泳考试才能毕业，考虑到 1977 年，42% 的大学有某种游泳要求，这是一个巨大的转变。到 1982 年，这一数字已骤降至 8%，而如今，这样的大学屈指可数。

paragraphs.sourceText: Three Ivy League colleges — Columbia and Cornell universities and Dartmouth College — still require their students to pass a swim test before graduation. So do Washington and Lee University in Virginia, and Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
paragraphs.translationZh: 三所常春藤盟校——哥伦比亚大学、康奈尔大学以及达特茅斯学院——仍然要求学生在毕业前通过游泳考试。弗吉尼亚州的华盛顿与李大学和麻省理工学院也是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: Jeremy Manier, a university spokesman, said the reason for the change was to give students options in how they choose to exercise. To facilitate that model, the Fit Chicago program — which used to cost students $4 to $5 a class — is now free.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学发言人杰里米·马尼尔(Jeremy Manier)表示，这一改变的原因是让学生可以选择锻炼方式。为了促进这一模式的发展，Fit Chicago 项目（过去每堂课的费用为 4 至 5 美元）现在免费。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many University of Chicago students agree with the change, including Jim Foster, who is the student government’s vice president for student affairs. In his opinion, the swim test was outdated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多芝加哥大学的学生都同意这一改变，其中包括学生会负责学生事务的副主席吉姆·福斯特(Jim Foster)。在他看来，游泳测试已经过时了。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There’s that fringe sect of universities that say it’s a valuable life skill, but then again, so is self- defense,” Foster said. “So I think it’s a smart decision to really leave it up to the students to decide when, if at all, they would like to take the time to learn that skill.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “大学里有一些边缘派别说这是一项宝贵的生活技能，但话又说回来，自卫也是如此，”福斯特说。 “所以我认为，让学生自己决定何时（如果有的话）愿意花时间学习这项技能是一个明智的决定。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The “diverse needs” of University of Chicago’s campus is one of the reasons Karen Coleman, Vice President of Campus Life, cited for nixing the swim tests in a letter to students. “Ending (these requirements) will give us more opportunities to provide desired athletic and fitness options and give students more flexibility in how and when they engage in fitness, recreation or athletic activities,” Coleman wrote.
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥大学校园的“多样化需求”是校园生活副校长凯伦·科尔曼在给学生的信中取消游泳测试的原因之一。科尔曼写道：“结束（这些要求）将使我们有更多机会提供所需的运动和健身选择，并让学生在参与健身、娱乐或体育活动的方式和时间上更加灵活。”

paragraphs.sourceText: What Bilingualism Is NOT
paragraphs.translationZh: 双语不是什么

paragraphs.sourceText: I have had the chance to live and work for extended periods of time in at least three countries, the United States, Switzerland, and also France, and as a researcher on bilingualism, has allowed me to learn a lot about my topic (1) of interest. I have found that people there share many misconceptions about bilingualism and bilinguals. However, they also seem to have very country-specific attitudes towards it. (2)
paragraphs.translationZh: 我有机会在至少三个国家（美国、瑞士和法国）长期生活和工作，作为双语研究人员，这让我学到了很多关于我感兴趣的主题（1）的知识。我发现那里的人们对双语和双语者有很多误解。然而，他们对此似乎也有非常特定国家的态度。 (2)

paragraphs.sourceText: Among shared misunderstandings, one is that bilingualism is a rather uncommon phenomenon. And in fact, it has been estimated that more than (3) 50% world population is bilingual, and uses two or more languages in the (4) everyday life. Bilingualism is found in all parts of the world, at all levels of society, and in all age groups.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在共同的误解中，其中一个是双语是一种相当罕见的现象。事实上，据估计，超过 (3) 50% 的世界人口是双语的，并且在 (4) 日常生活中使用两种或多种语言。双语现象存在于世界各地、社会各个阶层和各个年龄段。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another misconception is that bilinguals have equitable knowledge of (5) their languages. In fact, bilinguals know their languages to the level that they need them and many are dominant at just one of them. (6)
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一个误解是双语者对（5）他们的语言有公平的了解。事实上，双语者对自己语言的了解达到了他们需要的程度，而且许多人只精通其中一种语言。 (6)

paragraphs.sourceText: There are also the myths that real bilinguals do not have an accent in their different languages and that they are excellent all-around translators. This is far from true. Having an accent or not does not make one more or (7) less bilingual, and bilinguals often have difficulties translating specialized language.
paragraphs.translationZh: 还有一些神话认为，真正的双语者在不同语言中没有口音，并且他们是优秀的全能翻译家。这远非事实。有口音与否并不会使双语能力增加或减少（7），而且双语者在翻译专业语言时通常会遇到困难。

paragraphs.sourceText: Then there is the misconception all bilinguals are bicultural and that (8) they have double personalities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 还有一种误解是，所有双语者都是双文化的，并且 (8) 他们具有双重人格。

paragraphs.sourceText: As concerning children, many worries and misconceptions are also (9) widespread. The first is that bilingualism will suspend language acquisition (10) in young children. This was a popular myth in the first part of the last century, but there is no research evidence to that effect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 关于儿童，许多担忧和误解也普遍存在(9)。首先，双语会阻碍幼儿的语言习得（10）。这是上世纪上半叶流行的神话，但没有研究证据证明这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: Multilingualism is the natural potential available to every normal human being rather than an unusual exception. It need not require the ability to speak two unrelated languages; a user of the literacy and a dialectal variety is already multicompetent. In the (1) meantime, multicompetence does not require perfect fluency in all the languages in one’s command; thus, setting the boundary would (2) probably be a mission incomplete. (3)
paragraphs.translationZh: 多语言能力是每个正常人的自然潜力，而不是一个不寻常的例外。它不需要具备说两种不相关语言的能力；识字和方言多样性的使用者已经具有多种能力。同时，（1）同时，多重能力并不要求完美流利地掌握一个人所掌握的所有语言；因此，设定边界（2）可能是一项未完成的任务。 (3)

paragraphs.sourceText: The advantages that multilinguals exhibit over monolinguals are not restricted to linguistic knowledge only, and extend outside (4) the area of language. Children and older persons learning foreign languages demonstrate a keener awareness and a sharp perception (5) of language, are more efficient communicators in their mother tongue, and have a better ear for listening and longer memories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 多语言者相对于单语者所表现出的优势不仅限于语言知识，还延伸到 (4) 语言领域之外。学习外语的儿童和老年人对语言表现出更敏锐的意识和敏锐的感知（5），是更有效的母语沟通者，并且有更好的听力和更长的记忆力。

paragraphs.sourceText: A person who speaks multiple languages has a stereoscopic vision of the world from two or more perceptions, thus becoming (6) more flexible in their thinking, and learning to read more easily. Multilinguals, however, are not restricted to a single worldview, (7) but also have a better understanding that other outlooks are possible. Indeed, this has always seen as one of the main (8) educational advantages of language learning. Multilinguals can expand their personal horizons and — being simultaneously insiders or outsiders — see their own culture from a new angle (9) that is unavailable to monolinguals, and enabling the comparison, (10) contrast, and understanding of cultural concepts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 会说多种语言的人可以从两种或多种感知中对世界产生立体视觉，从而变得（6）思维更加灵活，并且更容易学习阅读。然而，多语言者并不局限于单一的世界观（7），而且还可以更好地理解其他世界观的可能性。事实上，这一直被视为语言学习的主要 (8) 教育优势之一。多语言者可以拓展他们的个人视野——同时作为内部人士或外部人士——从单语言者无法企及的新角度（9）看待自己的文化，并能够进行比较、（10）对比和理解文化概念。
